newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - London Int rebuilding profits.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - London Int rebuilding profits.

text.p: Condom and rubber glove maker London International Group Plc said on Thursday it was on target to rebuild its profitability on a firm basis by the middle of 1997.

In a telephone interview with Reuters following the announcement of interim results, chief executive Nick Hodges said he was confident the group would see operating profit margins rise above 15 percent next year, compared with 10.1 percent achieved in the year to March 1996.

Profitability at LIG, which is the world's biggest maker of condoms, is recovering gradually after collapsing in the 12 months ended March 1994, when the group posted a pretax loss of 175.1 million stg.
"We set a three-year plan from July 1994. By July 1997 it's my aim to return to the original level of profitablitity, but it will be built on firmer foundations than in 1994," Hodges said.

The group's pretax profit rose 46 percent to 9.5 million stg in the six months to Sept 30, before an expected one-off net charge of 8.2 million stg. The charge largely reflected the cost of reorganising the Aladan condom and examination glove business in the U.S. which was bought in April for $69.5 million.

Hodges said the charge cleared the decks for the rest of the year. Noting that analysts were predicting full-year pretax profit of between 35 and 38 million stg before exceptional items, Hodges added "we are relaxed about that."
The full benefits of the Aladan acquisition would not be felt until the second full year, Hodges said, with the group's factories being remodelled to produce a new range of specialist gloves.

LIG "aims to be a credible number two" in the U.S. condom market, building its market share organically through marketing and increased visibility of the Durex brand. Hodges said the group aimed to take a 30 percent share of the U.S. branded condom market, where its lies second to the domestic player Carter-Wallcae Inc.
"That is a good battle," Hodges said.
LIG is also firmly on the acquisition trail "anywhere in the world" where it can take a leading position, with the Far East of particular interest.
Hodges said further announcements on acquisitions were likely in the second half of the year.
